currentCard.prompt: Какой предмет одежды обычно имеет воротник, рукава и разрез спереди, а его длинный нижний край можно заправить в брюки или юбку?

answers.note: Рубашка-поло — облегающая одежда через голову, часто трикотажная, с отложным воротником или воротником-стойкой.
Первое зафиксированное словарём употребление слова shirt относится ко времени до XII века.
Свитер — вязаная или связанная крючком куртка либо пуловер.
Футболка обычно бывает хлопковой, с короткими рукавами и без воротника.

currentCard.explanation: Рубашка обычно имеет воротник, рукава и передний разрез; её длинный край можно заправить в брюки или юбку. Рубашка-поло обычно надевается через голову, свитер вяжут или вяжут крючком, а футболка обычно не имеет воротника.

However, the complete polo definition is a pullover type of shirt with collar/neck and sleeves; the current broad front-opening phrase does not distinguish a short polo placket from a full shirt opening. Tuckable lower edge likewise does not exclude polo. Intended key1 has dictionary support, but unique-key qualification is open as SHIRT_POLO_FRONT_OPENING_OVERLAP.

absoluteLevel.assessed: easy intended, subject to unique-key repair
absoluteLevel.ground: Recognizing an ordinary shirt from collar, sleeves, front opening and tuckable lower edge is common adult clothing knowledge without specialist fashion study. The retained garments are real and comparable. However, familiarity does not cure overlap with a polo also satisfying the stated broad features; the final exact row must be made unique while preserving EASY.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Merriam-Webster records the English word shirt as used before the12th century.
correctNoteExtraFact.ground: The prompt/key asks for a physical garment identity, not word history. The full first-known-use contextL81-L87 gives a concrete additional fact about the correct garment name. It is explicitly the English word, not an unsupported date for the Russian word or invention.

defects.finding: A polo shirt can also have a collar, sleeves, a short front neck slit/placket and a lower edge that can be tucked. The prompt says only front opening, without distinguishing a full front opening from a polo placket. The saved source itself defines polo as a type of shirt and pullover does not mean it can have no partial front slit. Thus the stated property bundle does not adequately exclude Рубашка-поло, even though the generic shirt entry is the author intended key.
defects.requiredFix: Make the question/row distinguish the intended ordinary shirt from the retained polo in a source-backed way. Do not infer from pullover alone that polo has no front opening of any kind, or add a full-length-opening universal without adequate context. Keep a plausible clothing row and frozen EASY/key1.
